actions.body: Traditional economic and game-theoretic views of convention often rely on hyper-rational models of individual behavior and common knowledge. However, work in behavioral economics and computational neuroscience suggests an alternative: dual-process frameworks where model-free reinforcement learning captures habitual and procedural learning. By applying multi-agent reinforcement learning to temporo-spatially extended games, research demonstrates that complex conventions and stable preference patterns can emerge from simple habit-forming mechanisms. Summary: Habits and stable preferences can develop naturally through reinforcement learning without needing explicit rules or hyper-rational planning.
actions.lede: Exploring how complex, large-scale conventions arise from model-free reinforcement learning.

actions.title: How Habits and Conventions Emerge Without Explicit Rules
